nodes.title: The Search for Genetic Material: Griffith to Hershey-Chase
points: 1. Griffith's Transformation Experiment (1928): Streptococcus pneumoniae (S-strain with smooth polysaccharide capsule is virulent/pathogenic; R-strain is non-capsulated and non-virulent). Heat-killed S-strain + Live R-strain killed mice and yielded live S-strain, proving existence of a 'Transforming Principle'.

2. Avery, MacLeod & McCarty (1944): Biochemical characterization of transforming principle. Proteases and RNases did NOT stop transformation; only DNase destroyed transforming activity, demonstrating that DNA is the genetic material.

3. Hershey-Chase Experiment (1952 - Unequivocal proof): Used Bacteriophage T2 and E. coli. Labeled viral protein coat with ³⁵S and viral DNA with ³²P. Following infection, blending, and centrifugation, radioactive ³²P was detected in bacterial pellet, while ³⁵S remained in supernatant, proving DNA is the hereditary material.

formulas.label: Griffith's experiment conclusion
formulas.expr: Heat-killed S-strain + Live R-strain → Live S-strain recovered (Transforming Principle)

formulas.label: Hershey-Chase isotopic labeling
formulas.expr: ³²P labels DNA (found in bacterial pellet) | ³⁵S labels Protein capsid (found in supernatant)

nodes.title: DNA Structure & Watson-Crick Double Helix Model
points: Nucleotide structure: Deoxyribose sugar + Nitrogenous base (N-glycosidic bond at C-1') + Phosphate group (phosphoester bond at C-5'). Nucleotides linked by 3'-5' phosphodiester bonds.
Watson & Crick Model (1953, based on Rosalind Franklin X-ray diffraction data):
1. Two antiparallel polynucleotide chains (5' → 3' and 3' → 5') coiled in right-handed double helix.
2. Sugar-phosphate backbones on exterior; nitrogenous bases stacked inside.
3. Complementary base pairing: Adenine pairs with Thymine via 2 hydrogen bonds (A = T); Guanine pairs with Cytosine via 3 hydrogen bonds (G ≡ C).
4. Dimensions: Diameter = 2.0 nm (20 Å); Pitch per complete turn = 3.4 nm (34 Å), containing ~10 base pairs; Distance between adjacent base pairs = 0.34 nm (3.4 Å).
Erwin Chargaff's Rules: In double-stranded DNA, A = T and G = C; (A + G) / (T + C) = 1.0.

formulas.label: Watson-Crick B-DNA dimensions
formulas.expr: Pitch = 3.4 nm (34 Å) | 10 bp per turn | Distance between bp = 0.34 nm | Diameter = 2.0 nm

formulas.label: Complementary hydrogen bonds
formulas.expr: A = T (2 hydrogen bonds) | G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds)

formulas.label: Chargaff's rules equation
formulas.expr: A = T and G = C; (A + G) / (T + C) = 1.0 (Purines = Pyrimidines in dsDNA)

nodes.title: Packaging of DNA Helix: Nucleosome Architecture
points: Human DNA packaging problem: Total diploid DNA length = 6.6 × 10⁹ bp × 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m/bp ≈ 2.24 meters, packed into a microscopic nucleus (~10⁻⁶ m diameter).
Histone octamer: Basic core proteins rich in positively charged Lysine and Arginine residues; consists of 2 molecules each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
Nucleosome core: Negatively charged double-stranded DNA wraps ~1.75 turns (~146-200 base pairs) around the histone octamer. H1 Linker histone seals DNA entry and exit points.
Chromatin folding hierarchy: 'Beads-on-a-string' (10 nm) → Solenoid fiber (30 nm) → Chromatin loops (300 nm) → Metaphase chromosome (scaffolded by Non-Histone Chromosomal NHC proteins).
Euchromatin vs Heterochromatin: Euchromatin is loosely packed, lightly stained, and transcriptionally active; Heterochromatin is densely packed, darkly stained, and transcriptionally inactive.

formulas.label: Human diploid DNA length calculation
formulas.expr: Length = 6.6 × 10⁹ bp × 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m/bp ≈ 2.24 meters

formulas.label: Nucleosome composition
formulas.expr: Histone octamer (2 of H2A, H2B, H3, H4) + ~200 bp wrapped DNA + 1 H1 Linker histone

formulas.label: Euchromatin vs Heterochromatin key
formulas.expr: Euchromatin = Lightly stained, loosely packed, active | Heterochromatin = Dark, dense, inactive

nodes.title: DNA Replication: Semi-Conservative Mechanism & Enzymes
points: Meselson & Stahl Experiment (1958): Cultured E. coli in ¹⁵NH₄Cl heavy isotope, then transferred to ¹⁴N medium. Density gradient centrifugation using CsCl confirmed semi-conservative replication: Gen 0 = 100% ¹⁵N-¹⁵N heavy; Gen 1 (20 min) = 100% ¹⁵N-¹⁴N intermediate hybrid; Gen 2 (40 min) = 50% ¹⁴N-¹⁴N light + 50% hybrid.

Replication machinery & enzymes: 1) Helicase: Unwinds DNA double helix breaking H-bonds; 2) Topoisomerase / Gyrase: Relieves torsional supercoiling tension; 3) SSBP: Prevents re-annealing of single strands; 4) RNA Primase: Synthesizes short RNA primer providing free 3'-OH; 5) DNA Polymerase III: Synthesizes new strand strictly in 5' → 3' direction.

Leading vs Lagging Strand: Leading strand synthesized continuously towards replication fork; Lagging strand synthesized discontinuously away from fork in short Okazaki fragments (1000-2000 bp), which are sealed by DNA Ligase.

formulas.label: Meselson-Stahl density centrifugation ratios
formulas.expr: Gen 0: 100% ¹⁵N-¹⁵N | Gen 1 (20 min): 100% ¹⁵N-¹⁴N hybrid | Gen 2 (40 min): 50% ¹⁴N-¹⁴N light + 50% hybrid

formulas.label: DNA replication directionality rule
formulas.expr: Polymerization strictly 5' → 3' (Leading strand: continuous | Lagging strand: Okazaki fragments)

nodes.title: Transcription in Prokaryotes and Eukaryotes
points: Central Dogma (Francis Crick): DNA → (Transcription) → mRNA → (Translation) → Protein.

Transcription unit: Promoter (RNA polymerase binding site), Structural gene, Terminator. Template strand has 3' → 5' polarity; Coding strand has 5' → 3' polarity (mRNA sequence matches coding strand with U in place of T).
Prokaryotic transcription: Single RNA polymerase requires Sigma factor (σ) for initiation and Rho factor (ρ) for termination.
Eukaryotic RNA Polymerases: RNA Pol I synthesizes 28S, 18S, 5.8S rRNA; RNA Pol II synthesizes hnRNA (precursor of mRNA); RNA Pol III synthesizes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNA.

Post-Transcriptional Processing of hnRNA: 1) Splicing (removal of non-coding introns and ligation of exons by spliceosomes); 2) Capping (addition of 7-methylguanosine triphosphate m⁷G to 5'-end); 3) Tailing / Polyadenylation (addition of 200-300 adenylate residues to 3'-end).

formulas.label: Central Dogma pathway
formulas.expr: DNA (Replication) → [Transcription] → mRNA → [Translation] → Protein

formulas.label: Reverse Central Dogma (Teminism)
formulas.expr: RNA → [Reverse Transcriptase] → cDNA → mRNA → Protein (discovered by Temin and Baltimore)

formulas.label: Eukaryotic RNA Polymerase division of labor
formulas.expr: RNA Pol I = 28S, 18S, 5.8S rRNA | RNA Pol II = hnRNA/mRNA | RNA Pol III = tRNA, 5S rRNA, snRNA

formulas.label: hnRNA post-transcriptional processing
formulas.expr: hnRNA → 5'-Capping (m⁷G) + Splicing (remove introns) + 3'-Polyadenylation (Poly-A tail) → mature mRNA

nodes.title: Genetic Code & tRNA Adapter Molecule
points: Salient features of Genetic Code (Nirenberg, Khorana, Holley): 1) Triplet code: 3 nitrogenous bases specify 1 amino acid (64 codons for 20 amino acids); 2) Degenerate: Most amino acids coded by multiple codons; 3) Unambiguous: 1 codon codes for only 1 specific amino acid; 4) Commaless & Non-overlapping; 5) Universal from bacteria to humans.
Initiator & Stop Codons: AUG is start codon (codes for Methionine); Stop codons (Nonsense codons) are UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber), UGA (Opal).

tRNA (Adapter molecule): 2D Cloverleaf model (Robert Holley) and 3D Inverted L-shape. Arms: 1) 3'-CCA end (amino acid acceptor arm); 2) Anticodon loop (complementary to mRNA codon); 3) DHU loop (aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase binding); 4) TΨC loop (ribosome attachment).
Wobble Hypothesis (Crick): Non-standard base pairing allowed at 3rd base of codon (5' position of anticodon), reducing number of required tRNAs.

formulas.label: Initiation and Stop codons
formulas.expr: Start: AUG (Methionine) | Stop: UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber), UGA (Opal)

formulas.label: Genetic code degeneracy
formulas.expr: 61 codons code for 20 amino acids + 3 stop codons = 64 total codons

formulas.label: tRNA cloverleaf arms
formulas.expr: 3'-CCA end: Amino acid binding | Anticodon loop: mRNA codon recognition | DHU & TΨC loops: Enzyme & ribosome binding

nodes.title: Translation: Mechanism of Protein Synthesis
points: 1. Activation of Amino Acid: Amino acid + ATP (Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase) → Aminoacyl-AMP-Enzyme + PPi; charged to tRNA forming Aminoacyl-tRNA.
2. Initiation: Small ribosomal subunit binds mRNA at 5' untranslated region (Shine-Dalgarno in prokaryotes). Initiator tRNA-Met binds AUG codon at P-site. Large subunit joins forming active ribosome.

3. Elongation: Ribosome moves 5' → 3' along mRNA. Next aminoacyl-tRNA binds at A-site. Peptidyl transferase (23S rRNA in prokaryotes, 28S rRNA in eukaryotes) catalyzes peptide bond formation between P-site and A-site amino acids. Translocation shifts ribosome 1 codon forward via EF-G; empty tRNA released through E-site.
4. Termination: Stop codon enters A-site; release factors bind, cleaving polypeptide chain from tRNA and disassembling ribosomal complex.

formulas.label: Amino acid charging equation
formulas.expr: Amino acid + ATP + tRNA (Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase) → Aminoacyl-tRNA + AMP + 2Pi

formulas.label: Peptide bond catalyst (Ribozyme)
formulas.expr: 23S rRNA in prokaryotes | 28S rRNA in eukaryotes (Peptidyl transferase activity)

formulas.label: Ribosomal sites functional order
formulas.expr: A-site (Aminoacyl arrival) → P-site (Peptide bond synthesis) → E-site (Exit of empty tRNA)

nodes.title: Regulation of Gene Expression: The Lac Operon
points: Lac Operon (Jacob & Monod, 1961 in E. coli): Model for transcriptional gene regulation in prokaryotes (inducible operon).

Components of Lac Operon: 1) Regulator gene (i-gene): Constitutively expresses Lac repressor protein; 2) Promoter (P): RNA polymerase binding site; 3) Operator (O): Repressor binding switch; 4) Structural genes: lac Z (β-galactosidase hydrolyzes lactose to glucose + galactose), lac Y (Permease facilitates lactose entry), lac A (Transacetylase transfers acetyl group).
Operon Switched OFF (in absence of lactose): Active repressor binds Operator, preventing RNA polymerase from transcribing structural genes.

Operon Switched ON (in presence of lactose): Inducer (Allolactose) binds repressor, causing conformational change; inactive repressor detaches from operator, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe lac Z, Y, A.

formulas.label: Lac operon structural genes and enzymes
formulas.expr: lac Z = β-Galactosidase | lac Y = Permease | lac A = Transacetylase

formulas.label: Lactose hydrolysis reaction
formulas.expr: Lactose + H₂O (β-Galactosidase) → D-Glucose + D-Galactose

formulas.label: Lac operon regulation state
formulas.expr: No Lactose: Repressor binds Operator → OFF | + Lactose: Allolactose binds Repressor → ON (Inducible system)

nodes.title: Human Genome Project & DNA Fingerprinting
points: Human Genome Project (HGP, 1990-2003): Mega project. Key findings: Human genome has 3.1647 × 10⁹ bp; ~30,000 genes; average gene size ~3000 bp (largest gene is Dystrophin: 2.4 million bp); Chromosome 1 has most genes (2968), Y has fewest (231); less than 2% genome codes for proteins; 1.4 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs).
DNA Fingerprinting (Alec Jeffreys; Lalji Singh in India): Relies on DNA polymorphism in non-coding VNTRs (Variable Number of Tandem Repeats / minisatellites).

DNA Fingerprinting steps: 1) Isolation of DNA → 2) Digestion with restriction endonucleases → 3) Separation by agarose gel electrophoresis → 4) Southern blotting onto nylon membrane → 5) Hybridization with radiolabeled VNTR probe → 6) Autoradiography detection yielding distinct band patterns.

formulas.label: Key HGP numerical statistics
formulas.expr: Total bp: 3.16 × 10⁹ | Total genes: ~30,000 | Coding genome: < 2% | Chr 1: 2968 genes | Chr Y: 231 genes

formulas.label: DNA fingerprinting workflow
formulas.expr: Isolation → Restriction Digestion → Gel Electrophoresis → Southern Blotting → VNTR Hybridization → Autoradiography

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Template vs Coding strand polarity: If coding strand is 5'-ATG-3', mRNA is 5'-AUG-3'. If template strand is 3'-TAC-5', mRNA is 5'-AUG-3'. Always orient 5' to 3'!
TRAP 2: Stop codons mnemonic: 'U Are Away (UAA), U Are Gone (UAG), U Go Away (UGA)'. No tRNAs exist for stop codons; release factors bind instead.
TRAP 3: Lac Operon 'i' gene does NOT mean inducer! 'i' stands for 'inhibitor' (codes for repressor protein). The real inducer is allolactose (lactose).
TRAP 4: Meselson & Stahl isotope: ¹⁵N is a HEAVY stable isotope of nitrogen, NOT a radioactive isotope! (Hershey-Chase used radioactive ³²P and ³⁵S).
TRAP 5: Ribozyme proof: 23S rRNA in bacteria acts as peptidyl transferase enzyme (proof that RNA can act as an enzyme!).

formulas.label: Stop codons mnemonic
formulas.expr: UAA (Ochre) | UAG (Amber) | UGA (Opal)

formulas.label: Lac operon gene layout order
formulas.expr: p - i - p - o - z - y - a ('i' = inhibitor/repressor gene, NOT inducer)

formulas.label: RNA-enzyme example
formulas.expr: Peptidyl transferase = 23S rRNA (prokaryotes) / 28S rRNA (eukaryotes)
